info.name: Marvel Heroes API
info.description: Versioned portfolio catalog API: characters, comics, stories and first-party session identity. Start with the local environment and run the requests in order. Public examples are synthetic; the application has no public hosted base URL in this collection. The repository OpenAPI 3.1 contract is authoritative.

item.name: Operation
item.description: Stateless probes. Readiness checks Redis and local catalog configuration, not PostgreSQL or live-provider availability.

request.description: Application process liveness.
Configured local dependencies are ready.

item.name: Catalog
item.description: Anonymous reads from the application's v1 contract. These runnable requests pin the curated local catalog. They do not call a comics provider.

request.description: Search by case-insensitive name prefix. The test saves the first returned ID for later requests.

exec: pm.test("Pagination and source are present", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.data).to.be.an('array'); pm.expect(b.meta.page).to.be.at.least(1); pm.expect(b.meta.total).to.be.at.least(b.data.length); pm.expect(b.meta.source).to.eql('local'); pm.expect(b.meta.cache.state).to.eql('fresh'); });

item.name: Identity (disposable loopback only)
item.description: Sanctum uses session cookies and CSRF, not Bearer tokens. This write flow is skipped unless explicitly enabled for a loopback test stack. Run in order with a fresh cookie jar.

request.description: Initializes the session cookie jar and saves the decoded XSRF cookie only for this run.

exec: if (pm.response.code === 204) { const value = pm.cookies.get('XSRF-TOKEN'); pm.test('CSRF cookie issued', () => pm.expect(value).to.be.a('string').and.not.empty); if (value) pm.variables.set('xsrf_token', decodeURIComponent(value)); }

request.description: Creates a disposable identity and establishes a session.

exec: pm.test("Registration creates the requested identity", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.data.email).to.eql(pm.variables.get('test_email')); pm.expect(b.data).not.to.have.property('password'); });

request.description: Returns the current identity while the session is valid.
Initializes the session cookie jar and saves the decoded XSRF cookie only for this run.

exec: if (pm.response.code === 204) { const value = pm.cookies.get('XSRF-TOKEN'); pm.test('CSRF cookie issued', () => pm.expect(value).to.be.a('string').and.not.empty); if (value) pm.variables.set('xsrf_token', decodeURIComponent(value)); }

request.description: Invalidates the session.
A logged-out session cannot read the identity.

exec: pm.test("Problem format and code", () => { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Content-Type')).to.include('application/problem+json'); const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql(pm.response.code); pm.expect(b.code).to.eql('unauthenticated'); pm.expect(b.request_id).to.eql(pm.response.headers.get('X-Request-ID')); });

request.description: Establishes a new session with the same disposable identity.

exec: pm.test("Login returns no bearer token", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.data.email).to.eql(pm.variables.get('test_email')); pm.expect(b).not.to.have.property('token'); });
